title: The two operators disagree by a full point on four games
detail: BAL@CAR is -2.5 at DraftKings and -3.5 at FanDuel; PIT@PHI is -4.5 and -5.5; LV@DEN is -10 and -9.5; TEN@DAL is -8.5 and -7.5. The desk publishes the median and both books. Which book should anchor the market column is an owner decision, and it moves the difference column by up to a point on those games.

title: nfl.com terms prohibit systematic retrieval without written consent
detail: Section 1.3 of the NFL.com terms permits personal, non-commercial, informational use and prohibits systematic retrieval of data to compile a collection or database absent express prior written consent. The desk therefore stores hashed, dated manual reads and does not run an unattended scraper against nfl.com.

title: Depth coverage is 1 of 32 clubs
detail: Only the Detroit Lions depth chart was read in full for this build. Every other club chart is recorded as NOT READ, and every depth rank, replacement name and ablation difference that would depend on it is blank. The deficiency matrix is therefore one worked example, not a matrix.

title: The solved home-field edge depends heavily on the window
detail: On the two-season window the home edge is +1.17 points. Fitted on all 28 seasons it is +2.18, and on the 2026 season alone it is -0.56. The shipped model uses the two-season window because that is the window whose ratings actually track scoring, but the home edge is clearly sensitive to the choice and is reported rather than smoothed.

title: Two clubs print no injuries at all, which is not the same as being healthy
detail: Cincinnati and Washington are printed by the official page as No Injuries Reported for Week 11. That is a statement about the report, not about the roster: a player on reserve appears on neither the report nor this desk's tables. Both clubs are shown with the official string rather than as zeroes.
blank_value_reason: all per-player counts for CIN and WAS are blank rather than zero

title: The pinned historical corpus is not an official NFL source
detail: The walk-forward and the closing-line benchmark use the committed nflverse corpus, a third-party dataset. It is used because no official machine-readable closing-line history exists. Its Week 10 2026 rows were reconciled 14 of 14 against today's official finals, which is the only cross-check available and is not a guarantee.
blank_value_reason: nothing; the source class is stated on every page that quotes it

title: A club depth chart prints position groups, not one starter
detail: The Detroit chart prints receiver twice as separate rows and several defensive positions with three or four names in one row. Treating the first column as the starter would invent a starter the club never named. The desk stores rows as printed and records the rank position within the group.

title: A rank-one player can be reported injured in a news item with no designation
detail: Today's official news feed carries a report that Detroit EDGE Aidan Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a significant knee injury, while the Week 11 injury report does not list him at all and the club chart still prints him first string. The desk records all three facts and does not convert a news item into a game status.
blank_value_reason: Hutchinson's game status stays blank because no designation was printed

title: The repository carries many overlapping desks that disagree
detail: More than forty NFL desks in this repository publish Week 11 numbers. Several print market columns this desk can now fill, and several print none. This desk does not edit any of them; it publishes its own numbers and records the duplication as a suggestion (SG08).

title: League average points per club is higher this season
detail: The shipped two-season fit puts mu at 22.44 points per club per game, while a 2026-only fit puts it at 23.35 and the 1999-2025 corpus averages about 21. Combined with a small home edge this makes the model's totals run above the market on several Week 11 games, which is visible in the difference column and is not corrected by hand.

title: Seven defects were found in this desk's own build, fixed, and are recorded
detail: (1) A league average left inside a margin expression inflated every predicted margin by about 22 points. (2) A plus-signed defence produced a defence column that correlated positively with points allowed. (3) Sum-to-zero by elimination parked the invariant on the last club alphabetically at -18.8. (4) Fitting on all 28 seasons produced ratings unrelated to this season's scoring. (5) A benchmark probability centred on the closing line produced an impossible +0.30 skill. (6) The fair line and the market line were in opposite sign conventions, inventing 23-point edges. (7) The corpus spread sign was read the wrong way round, giving a closing-line error no real line produces. All seven are now covered by tests.

title: Thursday kickoff falls inside this session
detail: Indianapolis at Houston kicks off at 20:15 ET on 2026-11-19, after this build. Any number published for it is a pre-kickoff opinion, not a result, and every price row carries the capture clock so that distinction cannot be lost later.

title: Two official pages give the Houston venue different names
detail: The game centre page prints RELIANT STADIUM, while the ticket links on the same site print NRG Stadium. Both strings are recorded against the fixture and the disagreement is published rather than resolved by preference.

title: The operator boards print kickoff minutes that differ from the official schedule
detail: FanDuel prints 1:01pm and 4:06pm for games the official schedule lists at 1:00pm and 4:05pm, and DraftKings prints 8:15 PM for the Thursday game while the official schedule prints 8:15 PM Eastern. The desk keeps the official schedule as the fixture truth and stores the board's own string beside the price so the difference is visible.
